Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Jim Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Laura Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Ruiz, Chief Operating Officer; David Lee, VP of Exploration; Anna Patel, VP of Marketing; and Emma Green, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Jim Harlan.

Jim Harlan: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q2 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved significant advancements in our future development plans and resource potential, bolstering our long-term inventory. I'm particularly pleased with our midstream segment performance, including robust transportation volumes and infrastructure expansions. We are focused on our production guidance for the next quarter and full year, accounting for key basin dynamics and efficiencies. Further, we are working on lifting costs per BOE through targeted trend improvements and cost reduction initiatives. We continue to adjust to optimal capital allocation priorities across dividends, share buybacks, and reinvestment. We are advancing our ESG initiatives with notable progress on emissions reduction targets. Finally, we are taking steps to capitalize on our EBITDA growth, reflecting strong year-over-year changes and underlying drivers.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Laura Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Laura Chen: Thank you, Jim. As Jim mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year. Operating income was $850 million, and net income was $650 million. We generated $1.4 billion in free cash flow and returned $550 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $5.2 billion in debt and $2.1 billion in cash.

Turning to our adjusted EBITDA, we posted $1.35 billion in the quarter, a solid 35% increase from $1 billion in Q2 2023. This continues a streak of robust growth quarters, highlighting the durability of our asset base despite market swings. On the revenue side, realized prices per BOE climbed 20% to $55, propelled by firmer oil benchmarks and tighter differentials. WTI held around $82 per barrel versus $74 last year, and our Permian pricing edged to only $1.10 below index—our tightest in recent memory—owing to new pipelines like Matterhorn Express and firm deals with Enterprise Products. NGLs advanced 25% to $29 per BOE on strong Mont Belvieu dynamics and petrochemical pull, while gas realizations stayed firm at $2.90 per Mcf with 60% hedged at solid levels.

Production hit 310,000 BOE per day, up 14% year-over-year, spearheaded by Permian output reaching 195,000 BOE/d—a 22% jump—via 32 new operated wells in the Delaware Del Norte area. These featured 13,000-foot laterals and custom diverters, pushing IP-30s to 2,300 BOE/d at 68% oil, exceeding expectations. Eagle Ford gas rose 10% to 48,000 MMcf/d, riding LNG ramps at Plaquemines.

Costs supported the upside, saving $170 million in EBITDA via sharp expense control. LOE fell 10% to $8.00 per BOE, aided by Permian electrification covering 45% of pads, cutting diesel 28%, and AI chemical optimization trimming water costs 20%. G&T fees improved to $4.30 per BOE from expanded EPIC Y-Grade JV. DD&A stayed at $17.50 per BOE on cheap reserve adds at $9 per BOE. Hedges added $90 million, buffering volatility from OPEC signals.

Permian fueled 78% of the growth with top-tier IRRs over 90% in Wolfcamp and Bone Spring. Gulf deepwater edged to 27,000 BOE/d post-Lucius tie-back, tempered by weather prep. Australian offshore steadied at 37,000 BOE/d with LNG price gains.

This fuels 65% FCF returns, including a $0.50 dividend—up 15%—and $450 million Q2 buybacks, $1.4 billion authorized left. Full-year EBITDA guided to $5.2 billion, up 27%, with $2.5-2.7 billion capex tilted Permian. Our 1,300-location queue at under-$45 breakevens offers years of optionality, plus Midland M&A pursuits.

Now, on production guidance for Q3 2024 and full year. Q3 targets 525,000-535,000 BOE/d, up 5% sequentially from Q2's 505,000 midpoint. Oil leads at 385,000-395,000 bbls/d, NGLs 67,000-72,000 bbls/d, gas 470-490 MMcf/d or 78-82 MBOE/d equivalent.

Full-year 2024 holds at 560,000-580,000 BOE/d, 11% above 2023's 505,000. Oil 415,000-435,000 bbls/d (76% mix), NGLs 72,000-77,000, gas 510-550 MMcf/d. Q4 trends higher before slight base drop balanced by completions.

Permian (76% output) eyes Q3 415,000-425,000 BOE/d, up 7%, with 25 frac crews versus 23 prior. Genesis fracs at 4,800 lbs/ft proppant and diverters yield IP30s of 1,850 BOE/d (86% oil), EURs 1.45 MMBOE on 12,500-ft laterals. But 9% declines on inventory need 230 completions (versus 210 last year). Service inflation up 6% QoQ and NM water issues loom, countered by 88% recycle rate and core acreage.

Eagle Ford flat-to-3% at 81,000-83,000 BOE/d, full-year +6% on seven rigs, channel fracs beating parent-child issues; IPs 1,250 BOE/d, 27% improved declines, 67 bbls/MMcf yields. Bakken steady 87,000 BOE/d full-year, Q3 41,000-43,000; plug-perf lifts EURs 12% to 950k BOE/well, gas constraints eased mid-year. GOM shelf Q3 26,000-28,000 BOE/d, +9% yearly on workovers, LOE to $7.50/BOE.

Macros: WTI $79 strip, LLS $81, HH $3.30 support $2.3B capex, 62% Permian. $5 oil drop trims 18k BOE/d. Efficiencies: MPD on 75% rigs cuts drill time 14% to 17 days; 15 rigs steady. Declines 10% (oil 8%), 11-year Tier 1 at $42 breakevens, Q2 adds 55k acres at $13k/acre.

Risks: storms, permitting; upside: 22k BOE/d nanoparticle EOR, tuck-ins. Capex $2.2-2.3B, 1.4x FCF at $76 WTI.

On capital allocation, with $2.5B YTD FCF toward $6B full-year at strips, we prioritize steadily. Base dividend first: quarterly $0.60/share, up 12%, 3.5% yield, payout 23% of CFO, $950M YTD, safe to $55 WTI. Five-year growth 50%, 90k shareholders.

Next, buybacks post-debt target $7.5B (from $11B): $3.8B authorized, $1.3B YTD at $70/share, 5% EPS boost. At 7.5x EV/EBITDA versus XLE 6.8x, accretive below $100 NAV/share. Like COP, retire 18% float; $1.2-1.7B H2 unless M&A like $1.5B Delaware deal.

Reinvestment 45% FCF, $2.9B capex on >22% ROCE at $72 oil. Permian 72%: 200 pads, 16k-ft laterals, cube comps 4,200 lbs/ft, IP30 +28%, 480 wells 2025 for 7% growth to 700k BOE/d, 56% oil. GOM 16%: Winterfell FPSO FID Q1, 160 MMBOE 2P at <$42 breakevens.

Intl 9%: Qatar North Field to 55k BOE/d by 2027 hedging Europe. Low-carbon 11%: $280M CCUS Permian EOR with Oxy DAC, blue H2. Permian 68% FCF, under Canada sands, over Gulf Brent. AI fracs cut D&C 12%, pumping $17k/stage.

Summary: div first, buybacks value, growth compound. $82 oil: 48% returns, 47% growth, 5% BS. Flexes dynamically; 280% TSR since 2021.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Ruiz for an operational update.

Mike Ruiz: Thank you, Laura. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 310,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Permian Wolfcamp wells online, which are expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Specifically on lifting costs—or LOE per BOE—this metric anchors our margins in choppy markets. Q2 landed at $9.20/BOE, 13% better sequentially from $10.60 and 18% below Q2 2023's $11.20. From 2022's $13 peak, we've trended down sharply, beating peer medians per S&P data.

Drivers: oil mix to 70%, gas deflation, diesel at $3.10/gal. Permian $7.50/BOE (-22% YoY) on pad scale; Eagle Ford $8.90 steady; Bakken $12.20 (-17%) post-logistics; GOM $17.90 from tie-backs, still sharp.

Initiatives: $1.3B program eyes 22-27% cuts to 2026 (~$2.10/BOE off). Digital (42%): AI maintenance via Landmark on 85% Permian, downtime -30% to 3.5%; Delfi twins on 55 Bakken pads, workovers -17%; drones cut inspections 38%, $0.50/BOE saved.

Ops/supply (37%): vendors to 42 post-merger, 14% leverage; Permian recycle 68% electrocoag vs Gradiant, skips $1.30/bbl fees; VFD ESPs 45%, power -25%.

Tech/portfolio (21%): stims/CTI on 18% Eagle Ford +28% runtime, defers $350M drills; 13k-ft laterals -20%/stage; divest Bakken highs for Permian.

FY guide $8.90-$9.40/BOE at $76 WTI. Upside CO2 EOR -$0.60; risks labor +$0.35. Low-end vs EOG/Conoco, FCF yield 20%.

Now I will turn it over to David Lee for an update on our exploration activities.

David Lee: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Delaware Basin and are planning to drill 12 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Diving deeper into our future development plans and resource potential, these underpin our enduring value. Our inventory ranks top-tier, with premium, economic assets yielding leading returns below $60 WTI.

Resource-wise, year-end 2023 PDP 1P reserves hit 1.25B BOE, total proved 2.9B BOE +16% YoY from drilling and Delaware adds. 2P at 5.3B BOE, 3P contingent >8.5B BOE. Replacement 225% production-based, 185% drillbit, SEC-booked with Ryder Scott audit at $66 WTI/$3.60 HH.

Diversified, 88% Tier 1 U.S. shale. Permian core: 470k net acres Midland/Delaware, 4.4B BOE 2P, 3,700 locations incl 1,300 Wolf A/B, 950 2nd Bone Spring. Eagle Ford 1.15B BOE, 78% oil Karnes. GOM 680MM BOE Shenandoah/Lobster like Anchor. North Sea Rosebank 20% stake w/Equinor/Suncor, 310MM net, FID oil 2027.

Development: $2.9B 2024 CapEx, 78% D&C for 330-350k BOE/d +13%, oil +20% to 230k bpd. To 470k by 2028 on 7,500 locations, 65% half-cycle $72 WTI.

Permian: 19 rigs/5 crews Q3, 12,500-ft laterals vs 10.5k, EUR +27% to 1.85MM BOE/Wolf, IP30 1,450 BOE/d, breakeven $34. D&C -20% to $620/ft via bulk sand, in-house mine 45% needs 32% below market.

Tech: SLB Delfi AI models -22% cycles, Wolf precision; Eagle nano-emul fracs +17% heights, +12% EUR Pearsall; CO2-EOR legacy +13% oil, 210MM BOE target. ESG: pads electric -42% S1, Pecos CCUS 1.1MT/y 2027, 45Q.

Tailwinds: OPEC tightens, LNG to 22 Bcf/d 2029 aids 27% NGL Eagle. Divested 55k DJ $420M to 32k Permian 3.2x NAV. M&A: $1.3B liquidity, no debt to 2028, sub-$11k/ac Northern Del like Oxy-Crown.

Challenges: services/reg, hedged 68% oil $73 floor. Discipline rules.

Decades growth, 16% NPV10 CAGR to 2030, compounding in tight supply.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Anna Patel to discuss our marketing strategy.

Anna Patel: Thank you, David. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for NGLs in the Gulf Coast, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact is significant.

Before that, let me update on our midstream segment, a key stabilizer providing reliable fee income against upstream swings. Q2 midstream EBITDA $480M, +14% YoY, 30% total. Utilization 94% vs EIA 86%.

Throughput 2.9 MMBOE/d, +16% YoY +6% QoQ. Crude 1.25 MMbpd +20%, Pecos Express 36" 570-mile Waha-GC at 97%, 880k bpd over capacity w/DRAs; Permian 6.7MMbpd, Exxon/Pioneer take-pay $1.30/bbl.

Gas 1.45 Bcf/d +15%, Appalachia Connector 980 MMcf/d 95%, FT rev +18% $130M at $2.80 HH. NGL Mont Belvieu 470k bpd +12%, margins $0.48/gal contango propane, Enterprise exports.

Permian 58%, Gulf 27%, Bakken 260k bpd post-DAPL, rail <4%. Eagle Ford declines hedged 72% vs $2 WTI disc.

Infra: $1.3B 2024 capex, 62% >16% IRR. Permian Hwy2 Ext $420M Kinder JV +210k bpd Q2 early FERC, 105-mile to 42" at $1.45/bbl Q4. Appalachia Link CS +320 MMcf/d Plaquemines feedgas. $270M digital SCADA/AI -24% downtime +9% eff. NGL Fractionator II 78% done +110k bpd 2026. CCUS pilots 550kt CO2/y IRA/DOE H2.

85% fee-based, 13-yr contracts 96% TOP/deficiency, 67% margins > ET 63%. Permian to 52%, $160M Bakken gather buy. FY EBITDA $1.9-2.0B, vols +13-15% Permian/LNG 15 Bcf/d 2026.

Funds 42% div/buyback.

I will now turn it over to Emma Green to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Emma Green: Thank you, Anna. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We have made significant progress on reducing our greenhouse gas emissions and are investing in renewable energy projects. We are also working to improve our water management practices and protect biodiversity.

Updating on ESG, especially emissions targets: sustainability drives value in energy transition. Net-zero S1/S2 by 2050, Paris/OGCI aligned.

2023: 24% absolute S1/S2 cut vs 2019 base, beating 22% goal; 4.5 MMtCO2e avoided (~950k cars). Intensity 17.8 kg/BOE -14% YoY, 38% below 2019. Methane abs -30%, intensity 0.21% gross gas <0.25% 2025 goal, vs Chevron/Shell.

Permian 47% prod: flaring -68% since 2021 to 0.3%, VRUs/midstream Enterprise saved 1.2 MMt +$160M NGL. North Sea: 2/4 platforms shore power Statkraft -42% or 0.9 MMt. Qatar JV turbine upgrades -17% 1.3 Bcf/d LNG.

Methane: 1,300 cont monitors Bridger GCI AI detects 1kg/hr 97% acc, 480 repairs 92kt prev. Electrif $850M to 2028: rigs/pumps -27% US onshore. CCUS Apex Permian Hub Oxy 1.6 MMt/y Phase2 5.5 MMt 2028 45Q. Gulf blue H2 pilot 12% blend Total Le Havre style 6-8% save.

Returns: eff $240M save 3.2:1 ROI, EU CBAM/SEC ready. MSCI A from BBB, $1.3B green bonds 45bps tight. 32% S1/S2 by 2030, $2.7B low-C 5-yr. S3: First Movers supp, 17% sold prod cut 2027 LNG meth/biofuels.

Leading responsibly, exceeding while growing FCF.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Tom Bradley with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Tom Bradley: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on lifting costs per BOE trends and initiatives?

Jim Harlan: Thanks, Tom. As Mike covered, we've driven impressive progress there—Q2 at $9.20/BOE with ongoing digital and supply chain wins positioning us for further drops ahead of peers.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong: Good morning. What are your expectations for production guidance factors?

Laura Chen: Good question, Lisa. Our Q3 and full-year ranges embed Permian ramps and efficiencies, with mitigants for declines and services, targeting steady growth as detailed.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Evans with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Evans: Could you please provide more color on operational cost reductions?

Mike Ruiz: Absolutely, Mark. Beyond LOE, our electrification and recycling are yielding broad efficiencies, supporting margin expansion across the portfolio.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

David Lee: Great point, Rachel. The resource adds and development momentum reinforce our multi-decade inventory, guiding disciplined growth and M&A selectivity.

Operator: Our next question comes from Peter Hale with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Peter Hale: What is the outlook for the midstream assets in the coming years?

Anna Patel: Thanks, Peter. Strong volume growth and expansions like Hwy2 position midstream for sustained EBITDA beats, hedging upstream effectively.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sofia Grant with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Sofia Grant: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Emma Green: Sure, Sofia. We're surpassing emissions milestones with tech like CCUS and monitoring, on pace for net-zero while delivering ROI-positive outcomes.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Jim Harlan for closing remarks.

Jim Harlan: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q2 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
